title: Configuring Border Gateway Protocols for VPN Service Edges

blocks.text: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) ensures high availability and fault tolerance by providing alternate paths to reach applications during Network Connector node failures and Network Connector to VPN Service Edge path or link failures. If a failure occurs in a Network Connector, VPN Service Edges use BGP to automatically reroute traffic to another Network Connector within the same Network Connector group for the specific IP address subnet or FQDN to ensure continuous communication between the client and server.
VPN Service Edges have the maximum path set to 256 and ECMP enabled to support BGP.
To configure BGP for VPN Service Edges:

blocks.item: Go to Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > BGP Edge Configuration.
Local AS Number: Enter the local autonomous system number used by the router for bidirectional traffic for VPN Service Edges.
The value of the Local AS Number must be different for VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors.
Session Failure Detection: Select one of the following options to detect connection loss:

BGP Timers: Enable to send keepalive messages between peers (VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors, and data centers) to determine if a path or link failure has occurred. BGP sends empty BGP keepalive messages over the TCP connection between two peers to ensure that the TCP session remains active.

From the Keepalive, HoldTimer drop-down menu, select how frequently keepalive messages are sent to peers (keepalive) and the number of seconds to wait for the keepalive messages to be received by peers before determining that the peer is down (holdtimer).

BFD: Enable to send packets between peers (VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors) to determine if a path or link failure has occurred. BFD is the fastest method for detecting failures between two systems by sending small BFD control packets between two peers. BFD sends the packets between peers in milliseconds compared to the seconds or minutes needed for BGP to exchange keepalive messages.

From the RX Interval, TX Interval, Detect Multiplier drop-down menu, select the number of milliseconds that should elapse before receiving a packet (RX interval), transmitting a packet (TX interval), and how many consecutive BFD packets can be dropped before determining that the peer is down (detect multiplier).
You must use the same session failure detection method for VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors for proper routing.
